provenance.input_format: Header: vertex_count and complement flag 0/1. Remaining lines: sorted unique 0-based a<b pairs. Pairs are original edges when flag=0 and missing edges when flag=1.
provenance.generator: Python random.Random(seed).random() in lexicographic a<b order; listed pair iff draw<listed_probability.

methodology: One instrumented findSquares call on each distinct graph, including adaptive membership/index setup and ordering. Graph generation, input parsing, Boost graph construction, and output verification are excluded from the internal search timer and separately reported where applicable. The search runs on one pinned CPU; no other performance suite should run concurrently. Counters add instrumentation overhead, so these times are diagnostic and are not additional end-to-end speedup measurements. Enumeration_checks sums wedge visits, wedge pair tests, and missing-edge pair tests; it excludes ordering, adjacency-structure setup, and support/component analysis. Every returned square is checked for validity and uniqueness; the count is checked using an independently implemented oracle. Sparse counts use bitset common-neighbor intersections. Dense counts use complement edge-pair inclusion/exclusion without enumerating all candidate missing-edge pairs. Fixed-alpha samples use p=alpha/sqrt(n); dense samples use p=1-complement_degree/(n-1). The experiment describes these families and supports, but does not prove, asymptotic claims. Those claims require separate mathematical analysis. All raw observations and input/build hashes are retained.
